content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions, mechanisms, and recommendations for monitoring or modifying therapy. 1. Cimetidine and Sulfamethoxazole: Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 2. Clarithromycin, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both clarithromycin and trimethoprim, as well as clarithromycin and sulfamethoxazole, prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified or closely monitored. 3. Clomipramine, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Clomipramine and sulfamethoxazole, as well as clomipramine and trimethoprim, increase the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases clomipramine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 4. Trimethoprim and Conjugated Estrogens: Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Close monitoring is advised. 5. Sulfamethoxazole and Conjugated Estrogens: Sulfamethoxazole similarly decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction also applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 6. Crofelermer and Trimethoprim: Crofelermer increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Crofelermer minimally inhibits systemic CYP3A4 due to low absorption. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Cyclopenthiazide, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Cyclopenthiazide increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 8. Cyclophosphamide and Trimethoprim: Cyclophosphamide increases trimethoprim levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, and close monitoring is advised. 9. Trimethoprim and Cyclosporine: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 10. Sulfamethoxazole and Cyclosporine: These drugs may enhance each other's nephrotoxic and/or ototoxic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 11. Dabrafenib and Trimethoprim: Dabrafenib decreases trimethoprim levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 12. Sulfamethoxazole and Dalteparin: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of dalteparin by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Alternative drugs should be considered. 13. Danazol and Trimethoprim: Danazol increases trimethoprim levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 14. Trimethoprim and Daprodustat: Trimethoprim increases daprodustat levels through an unspecified mechanism. Moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors increase daprodustat exposure, requiring a reduction in the starting dose of daprodustat by half. Hemoglobin levels should be monitored, and the dose adjusted accordingly. 15. Sulfamethoxazole and Dapsone: Co-administration increases systemic exposure to dapsone and its metabolites, potentially inducing methemoglobinemia. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 16. Desipramine, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both desipramine and sulfamethoxazole, as well as desipramine and trimethoprim, prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases desipramine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 17. Sulfamethoxazole and Diclofenac: Sulfamethoxazole increases diclofenac levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 18. Diflunisal and Sulfamethoxazole: Diflunisal increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, and close monitoring is recommended. 19. Digoxin, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole increase digoxin levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Trimethoprim also alters intestinal flora, affecting digoxin levels. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Sulfamethoxazole and Diltiazem: Sulfamethoxazole increases diltiazem levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 21. Disopyramide, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both disopyramide and trimethoprim, as well as disopyramide and sulfamethoxazole, prolong the QTc interval. Alternative drugs should be considered. 22. Disulfiram and Sulfamethoxazole: Disulfiram increases sulfamethoxazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is advised. 23. Dofetilide, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both dofetilide and trimethoprim, as well as dofetilide and sulfamethoxazole, prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole and dofetilide also compete for renal tubular clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 24. Dolasteron, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both dolasteron and trimethoprim, as well as dolasteron and sulfamethoxazole, prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 25. Dosulepin, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both dosulepin and sulfamethoxazole, as well as dosulepin and trimethoprim, prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases dosulepin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 26. Doxepin, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both doxepin and sulfamethoxazole, as well as doxepin and trimethoprim, prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole decreases doxepin levels through an unspecified mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended. 27. Sulfamethoxazole and Dronabinol: Sulfamethoxazole increases dronabinol levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP2C9 substrate. Caution and monitoring are advised. 28. Sulfamethoxazole and Dronedarone: Both sulfamethoxazole and dronedarone, as well as dronedarone and trimethoprim, prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 29. Droperidol, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both droperidol and trimethoprim, as well as droperidol and sulfamethoxazole, prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 30. Drospirenone, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Drospirenone increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. Drospirenone also increases trimethoprim levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 31. Efavirenz and Sulfamethoxazole: Efavirenz increases sulfamethoxazole levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 32. Elagolix and Trimethoprim: Elagolix decreases trimethoprim levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 33. Sulfamethoxazole and Eltrombopag: Sulfamethoxazole increases eltrombopag levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 34. Sulfamethoxazole and Eluxadoline: Sulfamethoxazole increases eluxadoline levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, caution and close monitoring are recommended. 35. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF and Trimethoprim: This combination increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 36. Trimethoprim and Enalapril: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 37. Encorafenib and Trimethoprim: Encorafenib affects CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 38. Sulfamethoxazole and Enoxaparin: Sulfamethoxazole increases enoxaparin effects by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Alternative drugs should be considered. 39. Epinephrine, Trimethoprim, and Sulfamethoxazole: Both epinephrine and trimethoprim, as well as epinephrine and sulfamethoxazole, prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 40. Trimethoprim and Eplerenone: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 41. Trimethoprim and Eprosartan: Both drugs increase serum potassium levels. Trimethoprim reduces urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially in high doses, renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 42. Erdafitinib and Trimethoprim: Erdafitinib increases trimethoprim levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 43. Sulfamethoxazole and Erdafitinib: Sulfamethoxazole increases erdafitinib levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Alternative drugs should be considered. 44. Sulfamethoxazole and Erythromycin: Both sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin, as well as erythromycin and trimethoprim, prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 45. Trimethoprim and Estradiol: Trimethoprim reduces estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Sulfamethoxazole and Estradiol: Sulfamethoxazole similarly decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction also applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 47. Trimethoprim and Estrogens (Conjugated Synthetic): Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Sulfamethoxazole and Estrogens (Conjugated Synthetic): Sulfamethoxazole similarly decreases the levels or effects of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction also applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 49. Trimethoprim and Estropipate: Trimethoprim reduces estropipate levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 50. Sulfamethoxazole and Estropipate: Sulfamethoxazole similarly decreases estropipate levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction also applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 51. Ethacrynic Acid and Sulfamethoxazole: Ethacrynic acid increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 52. Trimethoprim and Ethinylestradiol: Trimethoprim reduces ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Sulfamethoxazole and Ethinylestradiol: Sulfamethoxazole similarly decreases ethinylestradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction also applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 54. Sulfamethoxazole and Ethotoin: Sulfamethoxazole increases ethotoin levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 55. Trimethoprim and Etrasimod: Trimethoprim increases etrasimod levels through an unspecified mechanism. Increased exposure to etrasimod is expected in CYP2C9 poor metabolizers when co-administered with moderate-to-strong CYP2C8 inhibitors. Alternative drugs should be considered. 56. Sulfamethoxazole and Etravirine: Sulfamethoxazole increases etravirine levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Etravirine also increases sulfamethoxazole levels through the same mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended. 57. Fedratinib and Trimethoprim: Fedratinib increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are advised. 58. Felbamate and Sulfamethoxazole: Felbamate increases sulfamethoxazole levels through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance is unknown, so close monitoring is recommended.
